newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. Robotics unveils new 56 kilobit modem.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics unveils new 56 kilobit modem.

text.p: U.S. Robotics, the U.S.-based modem manufacturer, said on Wednesday that it has developed a new modem that can operate at 56 kilobits per second and has comparable speeds to ISDN networks.

U.S. Robotics, in a statement issued by its German public relations representative, said the x2 modem will begin field testing in November and will be delivered to customers beginning in the 1997 first quarter.
The fastest modem currently on the market is 33.6 kilobits per second (kbps).
U.S. Robotics said on Tuesday that it would introduce a new technology on Wednesday and analysts had believed it might be the long-awaited faster modem.
The company said it has currently signed up 32 on-line service providers to field test and market the modems, including America Online and IBM Global Network.
Customers who buy existing "Sporster" modems from U.S. Robotics will need simple and relatively inexpensive upgrades to existing modems. The upgrade will be available in January.
